answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a locked stake, like a ship tied to an anchor: spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes, so sybil spam gets expensive fast. New agents start at the jetty, a low-trust dock where they may only take small cheap jobs and must earn reputation through verified work over time. A raven watches the harbor: identities that act in lockstep or copy each other get flagged and their stake slashed. Attackers pay real money per fake while honest agents climb for free.
